reasoning: The claim that "lightning never strikes the same place twice" is a widespread myth and scientifically false. Lightning routinely strikes the same location multiple times, particularly tall, isolated, or conductive structures. According to meteorological agencies such as the National Weather Service, tall buildings like the Empire State Building are struck by lightning an average of 25 times per year (and have been struck dozens of times during a single storm). Furthermore, from a physics standpoint, a single cloud-to-ground lightning flash often consists of several distinct strokes that travel along the exact same ionized air channel within fractions of a second.
